segments: And there was in the city a certain emir whose name was 'Alam al-Din;
and this man opened the gates of the city before them,
and brought them in when no one at all was aware of him.
Rather, he brought them in, and went out and departed to the lord of Mardin,
and they took control of the city and devastated it.
They would come to a man,
while he himself and his wife and his children were sleeping together,
and immediately they would wake them up;
the man they would utterly slay,
and the woman and the children {OCR?} into bitter captivity—of the Huns, Persians, and Mongols {OCR?}—
And the youths, it is said, they slaughtered {OCR?}.
